feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications leader: the progression at NACo is clear, the scope is substantial, and the profile aligns well with strategy, platforms, and operations roles. Writing is polished and professional overall, but impact would improve with tighter formatting, fewer repeated skill sections, and more quantified outcomes beyond activity/scope.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression within one organization, showing increasing responsibility from coordinator to director to consultant.  
- Strong credibility through concrete scale indicators: 10,000+ page migration, 3.5 million annual page views, 50+ internal publishers, and broad platform/tool expertise.  
- Writing is generally concise, confident, and audience-appropriate, with a strong executive summary and consistent mission-driven positioning.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more outcome-focused metrics: several bullets describe responsibilities well but not results (e.g., growth, engagement, efficiency, adoption, cost savings, or campaign performance).  
- Reduce redundancy across “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; these sections overlap and dilute impact. Consolidating would improve structure and scannability.  
- Minor style/grammar consistency issues: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “12+ years of experience”; list punctuation is inconsistent (e.g., “web, email, social, and multimedia” vs no Oxford comma elsewhere); “French (A2/Learning)” reads awkwardly—use “French (A2, learning)” or “Elementary (A2) French.”
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear seniority and relevant scope. It reads well, but it’s slightly generic and overlaps heavily with Core Competencies and Topline Skills; adding sharper positioning and trimming repeated phrases would increase impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change to “12+ years of experience” and add “of” in “12 years of experience” for cleaner style.
- Lead with your current value proposition: digital strategy, platform modernization, and content operations for mission-driven/public-sector organizations.
- Replace broad lists (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”) with a tighter phrase like “multi-channel digital communications.”
- Consider rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience building and leading multi-channel communications, web modernization, and content operations for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel strategy, CMS and workflow design, advocacy messaging, and stakeholder coordination, with a strong track record of translating technical and policy issues into clear, accessible content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and “workflows and systems” repeat language already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- The channel list duplicates detail better shown in Work Experience.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Technical + IT sections. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing leadership-level capabilities will make it more distinctive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel, higher-impact phrasing: “Digital transformation strategy,” “Cross-channel communications leadership,” “Web platform and CMS management,” “Editorial operations and governance.”
- Replace vague items like “Multi-channel communication” and “Workflow & systems architecture” with more specific, senior-level terms tied to your experience.
- Consider a sharper version: Digital transformation strategy • Cross-channel communications leadership • Web platform and CMS management • Editorial operations and governance • Analytics, reporting and performance insights • Workflow and content systems design • Stakeholder and cross-functional leadership • Advocacy and policy communications • Multimedia and live event production
- Keep style consistent: use either “and” or “&” throughout, not both.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section substantially repeats the header summary and Topline Skills; keep it concise and avoid listing tools or detailed technical skills already covered elsewhere.
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” overlaps with Soft Skills and multiple experience bullets.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the NACo role below and Recent Projects. Tighten it around consulting-level outcomes, platform leadership, and 2–3 signature contributions.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + client value: “Advise a national U.S. membership association on digital strategy, Drupal platform enhancement, content operations, and enterprise web modernization.”
- Replace generic verbs with outcome-oriented phrasing: “Designed and implemented cross-functional workflows, analytics, and governance practices to improve coordinated communications across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Consolidate build work into one bullet: “Built campaign microsites, modular storytelling components, and downloadable member toolkits in Drupal; provided front-end implementation and technical support for public-facing web properties.”
- Keep AI search as the differentiator and add metrics if possible: “Led an AI-enabled search initiative, defining retrieval strategy, structured content models, and discovery UX to improve findability of complex content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance, workflows, analytics” repeats the Director of Digital Media entry; emphasize advisory/consulting impact here.
- Specific microsite/search examples also appear in Recent Projects; avoid repeating identical detail.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale signals. It should be tightened to foreground the biggest outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management points already covered in adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit
- Open with scope + leadership: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function, overseeing web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget.”
- Prioritize the strongest achievements in 4–5 bullets: website migration, analytics stack, in-house studio, governance/operations, channel reach.
- Make outcomes more concrete where possible: add team size, budget, % efficiency gains, reporting adoption, production volume, engagement growth, or cost savings from the studio.
- Suggested phrasing: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this higher-level and outcome-focused.
- Video-program language overlaps with earlier NACo entries; emphasize building the studio and expanding organizational capacity instead.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry reads generic and overlaps with both the later Director role and the earlier Digital Media Manager/Producer role. Tighten it around operational leadership, newsletter ownership, and establishing repeatable advocacy video/editorial systems.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize scope and function: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, improving editorial coordination and advocacy publishing.”
- Make bullets more outcome-led and parallel:
- “Owned production of four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- “Launched and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- “Built stronger editorial planning across communications, advocacy and program teams, improving alignment and publishing consistency.”
- “Standardized digital publishing workflows to improve coordination, turnaround time and content quality.”
- If possible, add metrics: open rates, video views, publishing volume, turnaround-time reduction, or stakeholder/team count.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update” overlaps with the 2015–2018 role and the footer project; keep this version focused on scaling/operationalizing it.
- “Improved workflows/editorial coordination” overlaps with the 2022–2024 Director role; avoid broad governance language here.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies and reads generic rather than differentiated. Tighten it to emphasize senior leadership scope and public-sector relevance without repeating adjacent sections.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less repetitive phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial governance and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy communications
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Consider swapping “content planning” for “content operations” or “content strategy,” which better matches the seniority shown in recent roles.
- If space allows, make one phrase more outcome-oriented, e.g. “Editorial governance for high-volume publishing” or “Enterprise content operations for complex organizations.”
- Keep terminology aligned with recent experience: “cross-channel” may be stronger than “multi-channel” given web, email, social, video, and AI search work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with “Advocacy and public-sector communications”; use one version consistently.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it’s too tool-heavy and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and recent execution themes, not repeat a software inventory.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability areas tied to recent work: “Drupal platform leadership,” “CMS modernization,” “front-end implementation,” “API and workflow integration,” “AI-enabled search.”
- Cut lower-signal or older items here (e.g., jQuery, Airtable systems) unless they are central to target roles.
- Use grouped phrasing instead of a long list, e.g.: “Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint & Power Pages • CMS modernization & front-end implementation • API integrations & workflow automation • AI-enabled search experiences”
- If possible, align wording to impact shown elsewhere: “Drupal platform development for large public-facing sites” or “enterprise web modernization.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates the detailed tool lists in “Technical + IT”; keep this version strategic and condensed.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” already appears in Core Competencies, so avoid overemphasizing it here unless it’s a target-role differentiator.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize strategic analytics capability, not repeat software names.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool list to value-led skill cluster: “Analytics strategy, KPI design, executive reporting, SEO/performance analysis.”
- Keep only the most differentiating tools and group them: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio/Power BI, Microsoft Clarity.”
- Tighten phrasing to show seniority: replace “Leadership reporting” with “Executive dashboarding and decision support.”
- Suggested rewrite: “Analytics strategy and KPI design • Executive dashboarding and decision support • GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity • SEO and digital performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Technical + IT > Data, Analytics & Optimization”; use Topline Skills for strategic framing and leave the fuller tool list in Technical + IT.
- “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” already appears in Core Competencies, so avoid repeating that exact wording.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery

- Video production and editing

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill area, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize operational leadership and production capability rather than listing basic tasks/tools.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe for impact and seniority: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • In-house studio operations • PTZ camera and multi-camera workflows • Virtual event production”
- Replace “Video production and editing” with a more differentiated phrase like “Broadcast-quality video production” or “End-to-end video production” to better match the studio build and advocacy programming in recent roles.
- Consider grouping by outcome/function, not tools: production, livestream delivery, studio ops, event formats.
- If space allows, add scale/context in adjacent experience bullets rather than here (e.g., recurring advocacy programming, in-house studio build, livestream support).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestreaming” / “livestream operations” duplicates Core Competencies; use one phrasing consistently.
- PTZ camera systems is very tool-specific compared with the rest of the CV; keep only if targeting production-heavy roles.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it’s too bare and duplicates the stronger “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” skills section. This item should either add level/context or be tightened to emphasize the most credible, recent platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Prioritize strongest/recent tools first: “Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages” and consider dropping GitHub Pages unless used meaningfully in recent work.
- If space allows, add proficiency/context instead of a raw list, e.g. “Drupal (enterprise migrations, modular content architecture) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages.”
- Align wording with your recent experience: Drupal is clearly the lead platform, so make that hierarchy visible.
- Keep formatting consistent with other technical items; avoid overloading this line if detail already appears elsewhere.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists the same CMS platforms.
- “CMS modernization” in Topline Skills may make this item redundant unless this section adds specificity or proficiency.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools not already covered elsewhere and use cleaner, current phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: “Front-end implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery”
- Add specificity where true: “API integrations (REST/JSON), Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions”
- Consider dropping versioned labels (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) if space is tight: “HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery”
- If these tools drove outcomes in recent roles, move the strongest ones into experience bullets instead of listing them here (e.g., GTM for analytics deployment, Workers for performance/edge logic, GitHub Actions for deployment automation)

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” already appears under Topline Skills; avoid repeating the exact same phrasing.
- “API integrations” also overlaps with Topline Skills; keep it in one place unless you add more detail here.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow leadership. Since the CV already emphasizes automation and governance, this item should be tighter and grouped to signal systems design, not just familiarity.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe by function, e.g.: “Workflow automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Work management: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | Collaboration: Slack, Microsoft Teams”
- Consider dropping 1–2 lower-value/general tools unless they are current and used strategically; keep the strongest automation platforms first.
- If space allows, add a light qualifier to show depth: “workflow design, intake tracking, approvals, cross-team coordination.”
- Use “Microsoft Teams” instead of “Teams” for clarity and consistency.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” already appears in Core Competencies and Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrase verbatim here.
- Slack/Teams are common collaboration tools and may add little value unless central to your systems work.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as generic software inventory. Given the CV’s recent emphasis on leading email operations, this item should signal enterprise-scale campaign/CRM capability, not just tool familiarity.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing, CRM & Member Engagement**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp** only if all three were used meaningfully; otherwise prioritize the most recent/relevant platforms first.
- If space allows, add scope in brief: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (enterprise campaign automation) • Higher Logic (member communications) • Mailchimp (newsletter/campaign delivery)**
- Consider aligning terminology with work history: use **email automation**, **member engagement**, or **newsletter operations** to reinforce leadership-level ownership.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item overlaps with repeated “email newsletters reaching tens of thousands” in Work Experience; avoid adding audience-size claims here unless tied to a platform-specific achievement.
- “Engagement” may blur with analytics and multi-channel communications already covered elsewhere; keep this item platform-focused.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and specific to early-team building, platform refresh support, and multimedia production.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and progression: “Promoted through two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and support multi-channel communications across web, email, social and video.”
- Add clearer action/result framing: “Supported a major website refresh, improving publishing workflows and strengthening coordination across digital channels.”
- Tighten multimedia language: “Produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly video updates, expanding in-house multimedia capacity.”
- Clarify supervision without overstating: “Provided day-to-day direction and production support to a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the later “weekly advocacy video update” entry; differentiate this as the earlier launch/build phase.
- “Strengthening workflows” is repeated across multiple NACo roles; specify what changed if possible (publishing speed, coordination, or content volume).

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and underplays the strongest differentiator: launching NACo’s first podcast. Since later roles already cover broad digital/media leadership, this item should emphasize innovation/program support plus the “first” achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground the standout result: “Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities, while expanding digital storytelling and multimedia communications.”
- Make the podcast line sharper and more outcome-oriented: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” with specific outputs if possible: web features, interviews, audio packages, reports, or multimedia assets.
- If you can quantify anything, add it: number of projects supported, episodes produced, stakeholders interviewed, or programs served.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating broad “digital content production and multimedia materials” language already covered more strongly in later NACo roles.
- Don’t overstate leadership here; save team/enterprise-scale language for the 2018–2024 positions.
